evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/lib/comparison-context.tsx:40 — the mount effect reads `localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY)` and does `const parsed = JSON.parse(stored); setListings(parsed);`. The surrounding try/catch (`:39`-`:45`) only guards against a `JSON.parse` *syntax* error (malformed JSON → the catch clears the key). It does NOT guard against VALID JSON of the wrong SHAPE: a stored value of `{}`, `"x"`, `42`, `null`, or an array of non-ListingSummary objects parses successfully and is handed straight to `setListings`, so React state (`listings: ListingSummary[]`) becomes a non-array / wrong-typed value with no runtime validation. That value then flows unguarded into the provider's consumers — `listings.length` and `listings.map(...)` in the comparison bar/drawer, plus `listingsRef.current = listings` (`:52`) — and a `.length`/`.map` on a non-array throws a TypeError at render, crashing the ComparisonProvider subtree (and therefore any page that mounts it) on the very next navigation after the storage entry is corrupted. The `expiresAt`/`JSON.parse` sibling in lib/auth-token.ts getSession has the same structural gap but is lower-risk because it RETURNS the value rather than pushing it into render state. Trigger requires a corrupted/extension-written localStorage value (same-origin, self-inflicted or a misbehaving browser extension), so this is a client-side robustness/crash-resilience gap, not a security boundary crossing — hence severity LOW (+1). NET-NEW vs backlog: distinct from code-review-reality-web-comparison-view-i18n (that is an i18n string gap in the comparison VIEW, not the context's persistence layer) and from the already-`done` code-review-reality-web-inline-tenant-json-xss (serialize-script/tenant bootstrap, a different file + mechanism). Suggested cloud-landable fix (frontend-only, verifiable with vitest): after `JSON.parse`, validate `Array.isArray(parsed)` and that each element has the minimal ListingSummary shape (e.g. a string `id`) before `setListings`; on a shape mismatch, treat it like the malformed-JSON case and `localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY)` + fall back to `[]`. Reachability traced statically (provider mount effect → setListings → consumer render); real-world corruption frequency not observable statically, hence confidence medium.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/lib/auth-api.ts:67 — `requestJson<T>` (the shared fetch wrapper behind login/register/updateProfile/etc.) ends its success path with `return (await response.json()) as T;`, which is OUTSIDE any try/catch. The three preceding paths are all defensively typed: the network/fetch failure is caught (`:47`-`:49`) and rethrown as `AuthApiError(..., 'NETWORK_ERROR')`; the `!response.ok` branch (`:51`-`:61`) parses the error body inside its own try/catch and throws a typed `AuthApiError`; and `204 No Content` short-circuits to `undefined` (`:64`-`:65`). But a 2xx (non-204) response whose body is empty or not valid JSON — e.g. an upstream proxy/gateway emitting an empty `200`, a load-balancer health/short-circuit page, or an endpoint that returns `200` with no body where `204` was intended — makes `response.json()` throw a raw `SyntaxError` ("Unexpected end of JSON input") that is NOT wrapped in `AuthApiError` and NOT caught here. It propagates to callers (login form, profile update, etc.) as an untyped error, bypassing the app's uniform `AuthApiError`-based error surfacing and likely rendering a raw browser JSON-parse message to the user instead of a localized, coded auth error. This is an error-handling CONSISTENCY/robustness gap on a non-primary (empty-2xx) path rather than a correctness bug on the happy path, so severity LOW (+1). NET-NEW vs backlog: no existing reality-web finding touches auth-api.ts (the three open reality-web rows are comparison-view / realtor-mgmt / agency-errorstate i18n). Suggested cloud-landable fix (frontend-only, vitest-verifiable with a mocked empty-200 Response): wrap the final `response.json()` in try/catch and rethrow as `AuthApiError('Malformed response from server.', response.status, 'MALFORMED_RESPONSE')`, or read the body as text first and treat an empty body the same as `204`. Reachability traced statically (every exported auth call → postJson/requestJson → line 67); frequency of empty-2xx responses in practice not observable statically, hence confidence medium.
